answer: Make each join pay for how crowded its epoch already is. The k-th identity admitted in an epoch burns 100 x 1.15^k POA, counted on-chain and reset only at the close, so the price climbs like a terrace, one step per join. A lone agent arriving at a quiet wharf pays about 115 POA. A farm landing 50 keys in one epoch burns about 830,000; spreading them out trades POA for time, turning a falcon-fast swarm into a months-long climb. Agents still established after 26 epochs get half their burn back as stake.
